x: Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus in 1669 by boiling down urine, the first element with a known discoverer. Cavendish found hydrogen and Rutherford nitrogen.

t: Recall the chemists behind the Haber-Bosch process.

x: All three are correct: nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre, Bakelite the first synthetic plastic and Perkin's mauveine the first synthetic dye.

x: Phosphorus came in 1669, hydrogen 1766, oxygen 1771 and nitrogen 1772, giving B, D, C, A.
t: Recall the discovery years of elements.

x: Only fluorine is linked to Moissan. Chlorine is Scheele's, urea synthesis Wöhler's and Teflon Plunkett's.
t: Recall each chemist's discovery.

x: Moissan isolated fluorine in 1886 by electrolysing hydrogen fluoride with potassium hydrogen fluoride (KHF₂). Davy used molten salts for other metals.
t: Recall how fluorine was isolated.

x: Cobalt was found in 1735 (Brandt), nickel in 1751 (Cronstedt), manganese in 1774 (Scheele and Gahn) and molybdenum in 1778 (Scheele), giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the discovery years of metals.

x: Tungsten was found by the Elhuyar brothers in 1783, beryllium by Vauquelin in 1798 and platinum by Ulloa in South American ores, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Recall the discoverers of metals.

x: Both are true: phosphorus is the first element with a known discoverer, Hennig Brand, who found it in his laboratory.
t: Recall phosphorus as the first known discovery.

x: Both are true: Scheele and Priestley discovered oxygen independently in their own laboratories.
t: Recall the discoverers of oxygen.

Consider the following statements:
I. C.W. Scheele produced chlorine from manganese dioxide and hydrochloric acid.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: Scheele identified molybdenum in 1778, and Peter Jacob Hjelm later isolated the metal. Brandt found cobalt and Cronstedt nickel.
t: Discriminate discovery from isolation.

Consider the following statements:
I. Carbon dioxide was known as “fixed air.”
II. Carbon dioxide was investigated in magnesia experiments in Scotland during 1754–55.
III. J. Black conducted the magnesia experiments involving carbon dioxide.

t: Recall the inventors of early synthetic products.

t: Recall Lavoisier's contributions.

I. J.J. Berzelius researched rare earths and many elements.

t: Recall the impact of the Haber-Bosch process.

t: Recall Cavendish's work on water.

x: All three are correct: Seaborg's team found many transuranic elements, including plutonium, americium and curium, and proposed the actinide concept.
t: Recall Seaborg's contributions.

x: Lavoisier gave the law of conservation of mass, named oxygen and nitrogen and listed 33 elements, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii.
t: Match each item to its own description.

x: Berzelius created chemical symbols, the dualistic theory, many isolations and a systematised chemistry, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each item to its own description.

II. H. Moissan developed the electric furnace.

Assertion (A): H. Moissan received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1906.
Reason (R): The prize recognised his isolation of fluorine and his development of the electric furnace.

Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
